11-3031.00:21315.short: Analyse cost actuals per site and cost type to set next year's budget and reforecasts.

steps.what: Extract cost actuals, headcount and flex invoices
Map costs to sites, cost centres and drivers
Build budget scenarios: volumes, CAO wage steps, flex share, diesel
Challenge cost plans with site managers and FP&A
Set budget proposal for management team

11-3031.00:21315.design: A scheduled job loads AFAS ledger and headcount data and agency invoices into the data platform, maps them to sites and drivers by rule, and feeds a driver-based scenario model in Power BI with CAO wage steps, flex share and diesel as inputs. No model is needed at run time; unmapped cost lines go to the FP&A Analyst as an exception list.
11-3031.00:21315.previous_blocker: Flex costs sat in agency invoices outside AFAS cost centres, so mapping to sites and drivers was manual Excel work each cycle.
11-3031.00:21315.enabler_now: AI coding makes the mapping rules, connectors and scenario model fast to build and change.
11-3031.00:21315.still_hard: Agreeing driver assumptions with site managers, and keeping the mapping right when cost centres or agencies change.
11-3031.00:21315.human_edge: Weighing site managers' plans against the company's targets and deciding where to cut or invest.

ambition.what: A quarterly driver-based reforecast of flex and wage costs per site, instead of one yearly budget round.

11-3031.00:21315.altitude: The Finance Director spends budget time on challenge sessions and choices, not on building the cost base; they set the scenario drivers.

reach.learn: how HR headcount and agency hours join to finance cost centres

evidence.claim: Mature AI finance teams describe higher confidence but rising unclear ROI; budgets for usage-based AI overran by about 27%.
A driver-based scenario model in Power BI on AFAS data needs no model at run time.

assumptions: Agency invoices carry site and cost centre references
The CAO wage table can be kept as a reference table
unknowns: How the budget is built today and how many versions circulate
Whether site managers own their cost budgets
Share of flex cost in total staff cost per site
research_questions: Can 95% of agency invoice lines be mapped to a site and cost centre by rule?
How far did last year's budget miss on flex and wage costs?
Do site managers want quarterly reforecasts or see them as extra work?

11-3031.00:21321.short: Analyse actuals, forecasts and cash to judge Noordhaven's current and future financial position for management and board.

steps.what: Pull AFAS ledger, AR/AP, agency hours and bank balances into Excel
Refresh driver model: volumes, shifts, flex hours, fuel, margins, cash
Find variances against budget and last forecast, explain the drivers

loop.input: variance table above materiality threshold plus AFAS journal descriptions and site cost-centre notes
loop.output: one-line driver explanation per variance with the source lines it used
loop.check: every number in the text is matched against the variance table by code; lines without a source are flagged
loop.stop: one pass per variance, max two retries; if the check fails the line shows 'unexplained' for the FP&A Analyst
loop.why_not_simpler: the drivers sit in free-text journal descriptions and notes that rules cannot read

steps.what: Judge outlook and scenarios: fuel, interest, flex labour, customer loss
Write financial position memo for management team and board

11-3031.00:21321.design: Replace the FP&A Excel workbook that ties AFAS, the agency portals and Rabobank with a nightly Python job on a governed data platform. It feeds a Power BI rolling forecast and variance dashboard. A bounded model step drafts variance explanations that code checks against the numbers, and a template builds the memo skeleton.
11-3031.00:21321.previous_blocker: The agency portals and bank files had no clean link to AFAS, so every refresh was manual Excel work. Building and keeping integrations was too slow for a 10-person team.
11-3031.00:21321.enabler_now: AFAS Profit has GetConnectors and Rabobank delivers CAMT.053. AI coding makes small pipelines cheap to build. Model steps can read journal text and draft explanations whose numbers code can check.
11-3031.00:21321.still_hard: Volume and customer assumptions come from operations and sales, and those do not sit in any system. Scenario judgement stays with people. Agency portal exports may change format without warning.
11-3031.00:21321.human_edge: Deciding which risks matter, such as losing a large shipper, fuel spikes or CAO wage steps, and standing behind the outlook in front of the board and the bank.

ambition.what: A weekly re-forecast of P&L and 13-week cash, not a monthly one, with the director signing off a short outlook each Monday.

11-3031.00:21321.altitude: The director spends Monday reviewing a pre-built forecast and its explanations instead of chasing the workbook. They decide which drivers and thresholds the model uses.

reach.task: Maintaining the driver model and assumptions
reach.learn: How volume, shift and flex-hour drivers are built, so the director can test them directly.
Which accruals arrive late, because they limit how early the forecast can be trusted.

evidence.claim: Executive reporting takes about 32 hours a month, and AI-mature teams spend more on it, not less.
Data quality is the top barrier to finance AI (40.4%).
AFAS Profit exposes data via GetConnectors and Rabobank supports CAMT.053 statements.

assumptions: FP&A owns a driver-based Excel model today.
Power BI already reads a nightly AFAS extract and can be extended.
unknowns: Do the three agency portals offer an API or only CSV/PDF exports?
Is there a data platform under IT governance, or does Power BI hold the only copy?
Which operational volume data (WMS, TMS) is available, and from which system?
research_questions: Can FP&A explain 80% of monthly variances from journal text and cost-centre data alone?
Does a weekly re-forecast change any decision the management team takes?
How many hours a month does FP&A spend on the data pull today?

11-3031.00:21320.short: Prepare the board pack, annual accounts, bank covenant and statutory reports, then sign off and file them.

steps.what: Extract trial balance and closing data from AFAS
Build board pack, covenant calculation and accounts tables in Excel/Word
Write commentary and notes to the figures

loop.input: report tables, prior period commentary and variance notes
loop.check: code compares every figure and percentage in the text with the tables; mismatches block the draft
loop.stop: two attempts per section, then the section stays empty for the director
loop.why_not_simpler: the commentary is prose that changes each period; templates only cover the fixed parts

steps.what: Answer auditor and board questions, settle disclosures
Sign off and file: KVK via SBR, bank, CBS

11-3031.00:21320.design: A scheduled job reads the closed AFAS period into a reporting dataset and fills fixed templates for the board pack, the bank covenant calculation and the accounts tables, with a reconciliation check against the trial balance. A bounded model step drafts commentary whose numbers code checks. Filing to KVK goes through a separate SBR tool because AFAS cannot file for large companies, and every external submission needs the director's sign-off.
11-3031.00:21320.previous_blocker: Report layouts changed every period and were rebuilt by hand in Excel and Word. Statutory formats such as SBR need tooling outside AFAS.
11-3031.00:21320.enabler_now: AI coding makes template generators and reconciliation checks cheap to build and change. Model steps can draft commentary that code checks figure by figure.
11-3031.00:21320.still_hard: Disclosure judgement, auditor negotiation and new rules: CSRD applies only above 1,000 employees and €450 million turnover, and Dutch B2B e-invoicing reporting is coming from 2030–2031. Report volume tends to grow once reports are cheap to make.
11-3031.00:21320.human_edge: Signing the accounts and the covenant statement, judging disclosures with the auditor, and explaining the results to the board and the bank.
11-3031.00:21320.altitude: The director reviews a ready pack and writes only the key messages. They decide which reports exist and cap their number so the time saved is not spent on more reports.

reach.learn: Which audit adjustments recur, so checks can catch them before the pack is built.
The mapping from AFAS accounts to report lines, which the generator will own.

evidence.claim: Large companies file accounts with KVK via SBR from FY2025, and AFAS cannot do this for them.
CSRD now applies above 1,000 employees and €450 million turnover.
B2B e-invoicing from 1 July 2030 and digital reporting from 1 July 2031 are planned.
Workday's Accounting Agent prepares entries and leaves review and judgement with the team.
More AI-mature teams spend more hours on executive reporting.

assumptions: Noordhaven is a large company under Dutch law (BW 2:397) and files through SBR.
There is a bank facility with financial covenants reported each quarter.
unknowns: Turnover, which decides whether CSRD applies.
Which SBR filing tool or accountant files the accounts today?
Does the auditor accept generated tables with a reconciliation log as audit evidence?
research_questions: How many hours a quarter go into rebuilding the board pack layout?
Can the AFAS-to-report-line mapping stay stable across a full year?
Does the auditor's adjustment count fall after the generator and checks are in place?

11-3031.00:21317.short: Assess credit limit requests for new and growing shippers, and prepare bank facility applications and covenant files.

steps.what: Receive credit limit request from sales or collections by mail
Gather KvK extract, credit report, annual accounts, AFAS payment history
Analyse figures and draft limit proposal with terms

loop.input: filed annual accounts PDF and credit report of a legal entity
loop.output: key ratios (equity, current ratio, result) and red flags in a fixed form, with page references
loop.check: extracted totals must balance (assets = liabilities plus equity); mismatches send the file to manual entry
loop.stop: one extraction plus one retry; then manual. Sole traders (natural persons) skip the model and use rules only, to stay out of EU AI Act Annex III 5(b)
loop.why_not_simpler: filed accounts arrive as PDFs in varying layouts; the limit itself is computed by deterministic rules from the extracted ratios

steps.what: Decide limit, payment terms and any security
Record limit in AFAS and inform sales and customer

11-3031.00:21317.design: A request form in Teams/SharePoint starts a workflow that pulls the KvK extract, credit report and AFAS payment history into one credit file. Deterministic rules from the written credit policy compute a proposed limit. For legal entities a bounded model step extracts ratios from the filed accounts. The director approves in one screen, and the approved limit is written to the AFAS debtor record with a log entry.
11-3031.00:21317.previous_blocker: Credit data sat in PDFs, agency portals and AFAS screens, and the credit policy was mostly in the director's head. Too few requests came in to justify a credit tool.
11-3031.00:21317.enabler_now: KvK and credit agencies offer APIs, AFAS UpdateConnectors can set debtor limits, and model steps can read filed accounts PDFs with checks that the totals balance.
11-3031.00:21317.still_hard: Writing the credit policy as explicit rules. Sole-trader hauliers are natural persons, so model scoring would be high-risk under the EU AI Act and stays out. Small shippers rarely file useful accounts.
11-3031.00:21317.human_edge: Weighing commercial value against risk for a shipper, and agreeing security or shorter terms in a conversation with sales and the customer.

ambition.what: Review every shipper's credit limit each quarter against payment behaviour, not only when a new request arrives.

11-3031.00:21317.altitude: The director approves a prepared file in minutes instead of building it. They own the written credit policy and its thresholds, including which requests below a set amount the Collections Officer may approve alone.

reach.learn: Which payment patterns come before a default, so they can be written into the limit rules.
How limits and provisions connect at month end.

evidence.claim: Creditworthiness scoring of natural persons is high-risk under the EU AI Act.
A large company may not agree more than 30 days of payment terms with a small supplier.
Advisors say credit and cash allocation decisions need mandatory human approval with timestamped logs.
KvK and Dutch credit agencies offer data APIs.

assumptions: 'Loan applications' here means shipper credit limit requests and the bank facility file.
There are a few to tens of requests a week.
unknowns: Is there a written credit policy, and who may approve which amounts?
Which credit agency does Noordhaven subscribe to, and does the contract include API access?
How many shipper customers are sole traders?
research_questions: What share of credit requests could rules decide without changing the outcome the director would choose?
How often do filed accounts PDFs extract cleanly with balancing totals?
Have past bad debts shown early signals in AFAS payment history?

11-3031.00:21323.short: Review finance processes and controls and recommend changes to procedures, systems or budgets.

steps.what: Gather process metrics: close days, touchless invoices, DSO, audit adjustments
Walk through processes with controller, bookkeepers and collections
Map findings to control matrix, auditor letter and policies

loop.input: walk-through notes, auditor management letter, control matrix
loop.output: gap list linking each finding to a control id with a quoted source
loop.check: every gap cites a control id and a source line; Finance Director accepts or rejects each
loop.stop: one pass per document set; unmatched findings go to the list as 'no control'
loop.why_not_simpler: notes and the auditor letter are free text that a rule cannot map to controls

steps.what: Write recommendation memo with cost and effect

loop.output: memo draft in the house template
loop.check: figures are pulled by code, not written by the model; Finance Director edits
loop.stop: one draft, one redraft on request
loop.why_not_simpler: the argument text needs writing; the numbers do not

steps.what: Decide changes, present to management team, track follow-up

11-3031.00:21323.design: A finance process dashboard in Power BI on a nightly AFAS extract shows close days, touchless AP rate, DSO and audit adjustments per site. A bounded model step maps walk-through notes and the auditor letter to the control matrix, and drafts the memo with code-filled figures. The Finance Director decides and presents.
11-3031.00:21323.previous_blocker: Process metrics sat in separate AFAS screens and Excel files, so every review began with a week of gathering, and free-text findings could not be matched to controls by rule.
11-3031.00:21323.enabler_now: AI coding makes the AFAS extract and metric jobs cheap to build, and a model can map free-text findings to a control list with sources the reviewer can check.
11-3031.00:21323.still_hard: Judging which change is worth the disruption, and getting the team and the auditor to agree, stays slow human work.
11-3031.00:21323.human_edge: Knowing the team, the auditor and the business well enough to pick the two changes that will stick, and being accountable for the controls.

ambition.what: A quarterly control review per value stream (procure to pay, order to cash, record to report) instead of one yearly review after the audit.

11-3031.00:21323.altitude: Less time gathering numbers, more time in walk-throughs and decisions; the Finance Director gains a standing view of control health instead of a yearly snapshot.

reach.learn: which close steps cause audit adjustments and lost days

evidence.claim: Data quality is the top barrier to AI in finance (40.4%), and controls described by CFOs often do not reach managers.
Advisors recommend people on exceptions for reconciliation and AP, with timestamped logs and an AI governance lead in finance.
Power BI on a nightly AFAS extract can carry process metrics.

assumptions: The nightly AFAS extract can include AP invoice status and receivables ageing
The auditor's management letter is available as a document
unknowns: Whether a control matrix exists today
How many audit adjustments the last year-end had
Whether the auditor accepts model-assisted workpapers
research_questions: Can AFAS Profit expose touchless-invoice and close-step timestamps through its connectors?
Does the auditor accept a gap list drafted by a model if each line cites its source?
How many recommendations from the last two reviews were carried out?

11-3031.00:21314.short: Build the monthly operational and risk report pack for management from AFAS, bank and agency data.

steps.what: Pull figures from AFAS, Rabobank, agency portals into Excel
Check figures tie out to ledger and bank
Build tables and charts in the report pack
Write commentary on variances, cash and risks

loop.input: variances above threshold with driver data and prior-month notes
loop.output: short commentary per variance, capped at one page
loop.check: every number in the text is matched by code against the data set; Finance Director edits and signs
loop.stop: one draft per variance above threshold; below threshold no text
loop.why_not_simpler: explaining why a variance happened needs written text from mixed drivers

steps.what: Review, sign and send pack to management team

11-3031.00:21314.design: Replace the Excel pack that ties AFAS, Rabobank CAMT.053 and agency portal data with a scheduled Python job on a governed data platform that loads, ties out and flags breaks. It fills a fixed PowerPoint and Power BI pack, and a bounded model step drafts commentary only for variances above a set threshold. The Finance Director reviews and signs.
11-3031.00:21314.previous_blocker: Agency portals and bank files had no clean link to AFAS, so the pack was rebuilt by hand in Excel each month, and commentary needed a person to write it.
11-3031.00:21314.enabler_now: AI coding makes the connectors and tie-out checks cheap to build, and models can draft variance text that code checks against the numbers.
11-3031.00:21314.still_hard: Agency portal exports change format, and the time saved tends to return as more and longer reports unless the pack is capped.
11-3031.00:21314.human_edge: Deciding which risks management must hear about, and standing behind the numbers when asked.

ambition.what: A weekly cost and cash flash per site (Rotterdam, Tilburg, Venlo) instead of a monthly pack only.

11-3031.00:21314.altitude: The Finance Director edits and signs a pack instead of building it, and gains time to discuss risks with site managers; the cap on pack length becomes their decision.

reach.learn: which drivers explain most variances, so thresholds are set well

evidence.claim: Executive reporting takes about 32 hours a month, and the most AI-mature teams spend more, not less.
Workday's Accounting Agent prepares entries while accounting teams stay responsible for review; Noordhaven runs AFAS, not Workday.
Workpapers built in personal chatbots cannot be rebuilt by the auditor; give an approved tool.

assumptions: The three agency portals offer an export or API for hours and invoices
Rabobank statements are available as CAMT.053
unknowns: Who receives the pack today and how long it is
Whether a governed data platform exists or must be bought
Which risks the board wants reported
research_questions: Can all three agency portals deliver hours and invoices by API or a stable file?
How many hours per month does the pack take today across finance-director and fpa?
Would management accept a one-page commentary cap?

11-3031.00:21326.short: Review aging and collection reports to see overdue balances, DSO and which debtors need action.

steps.what: Export aging list from AFAS and format in Excel
Add dispute, promise-to-pay and contact status from mail and notes

loop.input: debtor emails in the shared collections mailbox linked to an AFAS debtor number
loop.output: status label (dispute, promise with date, no response, paid claim) with quoted sentence
loop.check: label must be from the fixed list and the date must parse; the Collections Officer confirms before it is stored in AFAS
loop.stop: one pass per mail; unclear mails are labelled 'needs reading'
loop.why_not_simpler: debtor replies are free text in Dutch and English

steps.what: Review top overdue debtors, DSO trend and site splits
Weekly talk with collections and controller on actions
Decide escalations: credit stop, legal, provision

11-3031.00:21326.design: Replace the weekly Excel aging pack with a Power BI collections page on the nightly AFAS extract, showing DSO, overdue by debtor and site, and dispute status. A bounded model step labels debtor mails in the shared collections mailbox, and the officer confirms the label before it goes into AFAS. A notification flags debtors that cross a set threshold to the director.
11-3031.00:21326.previous_blocker: Dispute and promise information lived in Outlook, not in AFAS, so the report needed manual notes every week.
11-3031.00:21326.enabler_now: Power BI already runs on AFAS data. Model steps can label Dutch and English mails reliably enough for a person to confirm with one click.
11-3031.00:21326.still_hard: Disputes often start in operations (damaged goods, waiting time) and reach finance late. The 30-day cap on payment terms for small suppliers applies on the payables side and needs its own check.
11-3031.00:21326.human_edge: Choosing when to stop deliveries to a large shipper and having that conversation with sales and the customer.

ambition.what: A forward cash-in forecast per week for the next 30 to 60 days, built from promises and payment patterns, instead of explaining DSO after the fact.

11-3031.00:21326.altitude: The director reads a live dashboard and only acts on flagged debtors. They set the escalation thresholds and decide the credit stops.

reach.learn: How disputes are recorded, so the labels match how the work is done.
Which invoice errors cause disputes, so they can be fixed at the source.

evidence.claim: 81% of Dutch finance professionals explain DSO after the fact; only 12% plan cash-in more than 30 days ahead.
Power BI can show aging and DSO from an AFAS extract.

assumptions: The AFAS extract includes open items with due dates.
unknowns: Are disputes recorded anywhere in AFAS today?
Does the works council need to agree to reading the shared mailbox with a model? Personal data of debtor contacts is processed under the AVG.
research_questions: What share of overdue amounts is caused by disputes rather than slow payment?
Does a mail label reach 90% agreement with the Collections Officer on a month of mail?
Would a weekly cash-in forecast change bank facility usage?

11-3031.00:21329.short: Follow diesel prices, interest rates, currency and supplier tariffs, and judge their effect on margin and cash.

steps.what: Collect diesel, Euribor, FX and supplier tariff data
Compare movements with fuel surcharge clauses and facility terms

loop.input: customer contracts and agency tariff PDFs
loop.output: surcharge formula, index, threshold and tariff per contract in a table
loop.check: each extracted field shows the quoted clause; a person confirms once per contract, then code applies it
loop.stop: one extraction per new or changed contract; unreadable clauses go to a manual list
loop.why_not_simpler: surcharge clauses and tariffs sit in varied PDF wording; once extracted, the calculation is plain code

steps.what: Summarise effect on margin and cash
Decide action: pass-through, rate hedge, renegotiation

11-3031.00:21329.design: A daily job fetches public diesel, Euribor and FX data and stores them on the data platform. A one-off bounded model step extracts surcharge and tariff terms from contracts into a reference table that a person confirms, after which code computes margin and interest exposure in a Power BI dashboard with alerts when an index crosses a contract threshold.
11-3031.00:21329.previous_blocker: Surcharge clauses and tariffs lived in PDF contracts, so linking market movements to Noordhaven's margin needed manual reading every time.
11-3031.00:21329.enabler_now: Models can extract clause terms with quotes for a person to confirm once, and AI coding makes the feeds and exposure calculation quick to build.
11-3031.00:21329.still_hard: Contracts with vague or negotiated surcharge terms, and deciding when to hedge or reprice, stay judgement calls.
11-3031.00:21329.human_edge: Deciding with commercial and the bank when to pass costs on, hedge rates or renegotiate, given customer relations.

ambition.what: A monthly fuel surcharge check per customer contract, so missed pass-through is caught within weeks instead of at year-end.

11-3031.00:21329.altitude: The Finance Director reads an exposure dashboard and alerts instead of collecting prices, and gains a fact base for pricing talks with commercial.

reach.learn: how fuel surcharges are billed and disputed by shippers

evidence.claim: In Noordhaven's context 'securities' means fuel, interest and currency, and 'credit lines' the bank facility.
Only 12% of Dutch finance professionals plan cash-in more than 30 days ahead.
Cash allocation and strategic purchases need mandatory human review and approval.

assumptions: Customer contracts carry fuel surcharge clauses tied to a public diesel index
The bank facility has a floating rate
unknowns: How many customer contracts have surcharge clauses and in what form
Whether Noordhaven has any currency exposure
Whether rate hedging is allowed under the facility
research_questions: What share of contracts have a machine-readable surcharge formula after extraction?
How much surcharge was not passed on last year?
Which public diesel index do the contracts reference?
